Le 13 septembre 1848, dans le Vermont, P: On 13 September 1848, in Vermont, Phineas Gage is preparing a blast on a railway site. The charge goes off too soon: an iron bar 1.1 m long and weighing 6 kg goes through his skull and destroys much of his left frontal lobe. He survives. His friends say he is "no longer Gage". But the accounts have greatly exaggerated: he would go on to drive stagecoaches in Chile, a demanding job, until shortly before his death in 1860.

Le 26 novembre 1872, Charles Darwin publ: On 26 November 1872, Charles Darwin publishes The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. He had sent a questionnaire to missionaries and travellers: do distant peoples show anger or fear with the same expressions? He also shows his family photos of faces electrically stimulated by Duchenne de Boulogne. His conclusion: the main expressions are shared, the legacy of a common evolution. The book quickly sells nearly 7,000 copies.

En 1879, à l'université de Leipzig, Wilh: In 1879, at the University of Leipzig, Wilhelm Wundt opens the first laboratory devoted entirely to psychology. Reaction times are measured there. Wundt distrusts naive introspection: observing oneself must be learned and done under experimental control. He would supervise 185 theses, 70 of them by foreign students, who spread everywhere. He is called the father of experimental psychology, a title he himself gave to Ernst Weber.

He notices that his dogs salivate before the meal, as soon as the lab assistant who feeds them arrives. He calls this "psychic secretion" and studies it: a metronome, then food, and soon the metronome alone brings on salivation. And the famous bell? It is not certain he ever used one.

A law was drawn from it: performance rises with arousal, then falls past a threshold, in an inverted U. For a simple task, more pressure helps; for a hard task, too much pressure brings you down.
